clue.text: The two of us saving money after chopping head off fish

indicators.note: saving in the sense of keeping safe, so the outer pair of letters holds the money inside it

parts.note: the two of us together are we

indicators.note: chopping the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: brass is informal British slang for money

explanation.surface: A couple economise by beheading a fish before cooking it.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money; 'saving' reads like thrift but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts, so it is a specific example.

clue.text: Intense anger surrounding new series

indicators.note: surrounding means the fury goes round the single letter

parts.note: rage is intense anger

explanation.surface: Furious fans greet a new television series.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a set or series, as in a product range.

clue.text: Sharp drop in deficit

parts.note: short can mean sharp or curt, as in a short reply
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A steep decline in the budget gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is an amount by which something falls short, a deficit.

clue.text: Mistake admitted by juror, really upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
admitted by means taken inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A juror concedes a blunder and is very distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Mistake admitted' as the definition, but 'admitted by' is the indicator that the letters are concealed in 'juror, really'; the definition is 'Mistake' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Very wise to cover one's face

indicators.note: the two outer pieces close around and cover the single letter between them

parts.note: a sage person is wise
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is, joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone very wise hides their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary synonym for a person's face or facial expression.

clue.text: Vetting, at sea, a French pontoon

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: Checking a French floating platform while out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game also called twenty-one or blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un, French for twenty-one, is the card game known in Britain as pontoon.

clue.text: The man wearing usual coat

indicators.note: wearing puts the pronoun inside the clothing, the other piece enclosing it

parts.note: set as in a set routine, the usual one
the man is he

explanation.surface: A man in his everyday coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of ice or paint is a thin layer, a coat.

clue.text: Place to eat grub, so apt abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A suitable spot for food while travelling overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub that specialises in good restaurant-style food.

clue.text: A bishop posted elsewhere

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
something posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A clergyman is reassigned to another diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, so they are somewhere else.

clue.text: Fictional detective Sam, seen originally in a suit

parts.note: Sam Spade is Dashiell Hammett's private eye in The Maltese Falcon

indicators.note: originally picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sam the private eye first appeared wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but means a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Writer about to move house

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the writer's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, so a writer
to go is to move

explanation.surface: An author is on the point of moving home.
explanation.walkthrough: House (or housey-housey) is the British name for the numbers game played in halls.
explanation.definitionFit: House is the old name, especially in the armed forces, for the numbers game also called bingo.

clue.text: As good as gold? Us almost

definitions.text: As good as gold? Us almost

parts.words: As good as gold? Us almost
parts.note: the finishers just behind the winner might say they were almost as good as the gold medallist

explanation.surface: A modest boast that we nearly behaved perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As good as gold' is an idiom for well-behaved, but here gold is the first-place medal; those placed second came close to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors finishing just behind the winner are the silver medallists, nearly but not quite at the top.

clue.text: Horse in flat race, not Ascot's first

parts.note: a flat surface is an even one

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out of the word before it

parts.note: to tear is to race or rush along

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the racecourse's name

explanation.surface: A horse running in a flat race, but not at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse. 'race' looks like a noun but is the verb tear; removing A leaves TER.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for the equestrian discipline of eventing, combining dressage, cross-country and jumping.

clue.text: Trio, initially, or duet, badly taught

indicators.note: initially selects the first letter of the word for a group of three
badly here means the letters are put together wrongly, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical group of three, or a pair, performed poorly when taught.
explanation.walkthrough: Trio and duet suggest music, but 'badly' acts only on the last two words, leaving the opening letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tutored is to be instructed privately, a close synonym of being taught.

clue.text: Scold manager when beaten in TT

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters between the two letters of the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: beaten in the sense of battered out of shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A team boss is told off after losing a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; 'beaten' suggests a defeat but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing woman, so a scold in the old sense of a nagging woman.

clue.text: Doctor and academic having part in complex procedure

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them
an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A medic and a scholar both play a part in a complicated operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, complicated and tedious process.

clue.text: Major road blocked by hostile heavy guns

indicators.note: blocked by means obstructed from within, so the unfriendly word sits inside the road

parts.note: an artery is a major road
ill as in ill will, hostile

explanation.surface: A main road is obstructed by enemy heavy weaponry.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large-calibre guns such as cannon and howitzers.

clue.text: Chronicler sneaks a look at broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: someone who sneaks a look peeps

explanation.surface: A historian sneaks a look at a radio or television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys, the 17th-century diarist, is said to have pronounced his name like peeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London, a chronicler of the Great Fire and plague.

clue.text: Quiet, living in a place such as Lincoln?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a resident is living in a place

explanation.surface: Someone quietly living in a place like the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth head of state of the United States, an example.

clue.text: Splendid beer knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back reads the drink in reverse order, as well as hinting at drinking it

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A fine beer is drunk down in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means fit for a king, so magnificent or splendid.

clue.text: Oppose all others across South Island

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the others enclose the two letters

parts.note: the rest are all the others

explanation.surface: Everyone else objects to crossing to New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or oppose.

clue.text: Can the German, leading strike in explosive situation?

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so these pieces go before the next one

parts.note: a tin is a can
der is a German word for the
to box is to strike with the fist

explanation.surface: Could a German be at the forefront of a strike in a tense standoff?
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox, literally a box of fire-lighting material, is figuratively a volatile situation ready to flare up.

clue.text: Persian ruler, former king, turned up trumps, ultimately

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ex means former
rex is Latin for king

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A former Persian king came up trumps in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I was a king of the Achaemenid Persian Empire who invaded Greece in 480 BC.

clue.text: Talk about a name for a dog

indicators.note: about means going round, so the talk surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a spiel is a glib piece of talk

explanation.surface: A chat about choosing what to call the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a breed of gundog with long drooping ears, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Rogue on the Spanish force

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rogue
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A villain makes the Spanish police force his own.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or force them into action.

clue.text: Father carrying in rope

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the parent's letters enclose the next word

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, used in old British slang

explanation.surface: Dad brings in a length of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rope' looks like a verb here but it names a nautical term.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is the rope attached to a boat's bow, used to tie it up.

clue.text: Difficult question for model

definitions.meaning: a puzzling problem or tricky question
a person who strikes poses for an artist or camera

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tricky puzzle to solve and someone who sits for a photographer or painter.

clue.text: Fine base — yours years ago

parts.note: fine thread is thin
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A fine foundation was yours long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic form of yours, used in older English.

clue.text: Late news: 'Jam following work on street'

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the previous piece
following means coming after the earlier pieces

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to jam is to press or squeeze

explanation.surface: A late headline says traffic is jammed after roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is late news inserted into a newspaper after printing has begun.

clue.text: Pick English literature course, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word for a programme of study

explanation.surface: Choosing an English literature degree, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best members, the elite or cream.

clue.text: Answer involving a repeat fixture

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the response wraps round the single letter

parts.note: a reply is an answer

explanation.surface: The answer brings in a repeat of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: In British football and other sports, a replay is a drawn match played again as a second fixture.

clue.text: Somewhat sooner

definitions.meaning: somewhat as in fairly or quite
sooner as in preferably, I would sooner stay

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to a certain degree, as in fairly cold, and preferably, as in would prefer to.
